result.title: Recoverable Symbols, Unstable Execution: Auditing Internal Pathways and Decision Identity in Visual State Tracking
result.summary: Visual features can retain every symbol a task needs while a model built on them still changes its answer when irrelevant parts of the image change. We study this gap in visual state tracking, where a recurrent executor reads a sequence of symbol tiles through a frozen ViT encoder and decides whether a displayed candidate equals the final state. Our diagnostic pairs each input with a donor view that preserves every queried tile, checks with a symbol-supervised decoder that the full symbol chain is recoverable from both feature sequences, and swaps individual internal channels of the same fitted executor in both directions. On 3,526 pairs in which every symbol is recovered in both views, changing the surrounding context lowers the balanced accuracy of a rotary recurrent head by 17.13 points. The loss runs mainly through the input-dependent rotation phase: restoring the original phase repairs 351 of 391 new errors and brings accuracy back to 88.54%, yet 142 individual predictions still differ from the original ones. A locked test on 192 unseen program families reproduces the pathway (28 of 29 new errors repaired; 382 of 384 predictions unchanged), and the effect partly carries over to single-image canvases. Consistency objectives derived from this analysis reduce the internal discrepancy they target but do not outperform ordinary data augmentation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究视觉状态跟踪中「符号可解码但答案随无关上下文改变」的落差：冻结 ViT 编码符号块序列，循环执行器判断候选是否等于末状态，并用 donor 视图、符号监督解码与同模型内部通道双向交换来审计；发现误差主要经由输入相关的旋转相位传导，恢复原相位能修复多数新错误，而由此导出的一致性目标并未超过普通数据增强。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接检验「内部状态可恢复不等于被稳定使用」这一关键假设，其符号可解码性检查与相位通道交换干预可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节保留、视觉旁路与 latent 内容因果作用的真实落差。
